issue_context.title: [types] Options accessed from module not extendable
comments: See https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.js/pull/9058#discussion_r602730487. In short, extend `NuxtOptions` and not `NuxtConfig` and you should be fine.

@danielroe @pi0 I've read #9058 and I haven't succeed to correctly understand what's going on 🙈

As far as I remember, modules need to extend `NuxtOptions` and not `NuxtConfig`.

And if I'm right, there was even a moment where `NuxtConfig` was a type and not an interface, and couldn't be extended.

The proper way is exactly what @danielroe mentioned in last comment, `NuxtOptions` should be extended.
Which will result on accessing `this.options.foo` through module definition but also have config key `foo` correctly typed.

The aim of `NuxtConfig` extending `Partial<NuxtOptions>` is to make any module options key, optional in project configurations.

Please point me out if there's something still wrong in types that I didn't get and should be fixed :)

I'd also say that the way to go is to extend `NuxtOptions` from the module's perspective.

`NuxtConfig` is still necessary and useful because it's needed if someone wants to annotate the config object in `nuxt.config.js` but I don't see why it should be recommended to extend `NuxtConfig` instead of `NuxtOptions`.

@kevinmarrec I agree. I think extending `NuxtOptions` is what we should be encouraging module authors to do (note: we should update the template which currently defaults to `NuxtConfig`). 

**Note**: we may take a different approach depending on how we handle Nuxt/module config in future @pi0.

Initially, we only had `Configuration` interface which was not considering options get normalized. This was leading to issue that internal typings was wrong because all `nuxt.options` keys was optional. Then we introduced `NuxtOptions` for internals (normalized by `options.js`) and `NuxtConfig` for `nuxt.config` interface with backward compatibility for `Configuration` interface.

Nuxt does not touches input options for custom keys and modules are responsible to merge it with defaults and should not solely depend on `this.options.moduleName` without normalizing. In other words `nuxt.options.i18n` is not a trusted source without explicitly normalized by module into a new variable. 

What I meant in https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt.js/pull/9058#discussion_r602729461 when sharing options is desired (like module A normalizing it's config back into `nuxt.options` for module B)

Nuxt kit will hopefully help on making it easier for defining modules and normalizing options but for time being, otherwise above is the case, please extend **`NuxtConfig`** for modules and not `NuxtOptions` otherwise it makes situation even harder to support all legacy cases.

I've reopened this issue to clarify this :)

Again, would like to talk about `this.options.i18n` rather than `this.nuxt.options.i18n`. Those are the same objects anyway, as you said, but `this.options` have proper types so it's clearer to reason about.

> In other words `nuxt.options.i18n` is not a trusted source without explicitly normalized by module into a new variable.

I either don't understand what you are saying or I just don't agree with it.

I'll describe the obvious stuff that we all already know, just so that we are on the same page:

The module can get passed options in two ways (typically):
- `modules: [ ['nuxt-i18n', { /* options */ }] ]`
- `i18n: { /* options */ }`

In the first case, the module receives options through the argument passed to the default export.
In the second case, the module has to access them through `this.options.i18n`.
In both cases the `i18n` options are unresolved.

Now, in the second case the `i18n` types are missing **inside the module** because `this.options` is `NuxtOptions` and not `NuxtConfig`.
I agree that it should be `NuxtOptions` because the Nuxt options themselves are resolved but then the module must extend `NuxtOptions` or else its types won't be available **to itself**.

If you don't agree with that then please say what's the plan to address that going forward?
I guess you must have some idea since you have a strong opinion that the modules should only extend `NuxtConfig` but haven't mentioned any alternative that would solve the aforementioned problem.

This is how it's done already.

My point was only about `this.options.i18n` missing types.

Your suggestion is now to extend the `Configuration` interface which yes, will work, but `Configuration` is deprecated so I want to be a good citizen and not use it anymore. Which leaves me with no proper way to do it if I'm not to extend `NuxtOptions`.

@rchl Updated reply (sorry it was a typo). indeed configuration is deprecated. And i18n not being available in nuxt.options is intended because it is not a nuxt option. What I'm trying to say is that module options should be resolved and typed internally.

That doesn't change the fact that:
 - `this.options.i18n` types are missing
 - the unresolved options are there

You can hide the fact that the types are missing by using `defu` or `deepMerge` or something, as it will accept `any` but technically the options are there but the types are not.

I'm not sure why you are saying that we shouldn't extend `NuxtOptions` in this case. Is it because of the compatibility problems associated with that? Would it be OK if we would somehow magically forget all the legacy types?

(Sorry about going on with that for so long. Maybe there is a bit of a language barrier or maybe I'm not communicating well enough...)

Thanks for your contribution to Nuxt!

review_comments: Modules receive resolved/normalized options which is `NuxtOptions`  (`Configuration`). If it is desired, the module author should directly extend `NuxtOptions` interface with normalized types or extending `Configuration` interface.
TIL. For some reason I had it in my head that this.nuxt.options was the normalised config. There's no point in this PR then - and in fact if following module template module authors should be fine.

That recommendation raises some questions in my head...

I understand the difference between unresolved and resolved options for **built-in Nuxt options**, but from the module's perspective, the types for a given module are never normalized/resolved because whatever user sets in the given module's options never gets updated to resolved/normalized values. Or rather they might, but only internally in the module, and the Nuxt config setting is never updated itself (at least not in the modules I know or maintain).

So from the module's perspective, it seems like the recommendation should be to always extend `NuxtOptions` rather than `NuxtConfig`. Is that true? That will make the types work both in MouduleThis and the nuxt.config.js itself.

Then I wonder what's the point of `NuxtConfig` interface... In which case will it make sense for a module to extend `NuxtConfig` rather than `NuxtOptions`? 

Also, if you are considering extending `Configuration` interface a viable option at all, then it shouldn't be deprecated probably. But then, I don't quite see the use case for doing that in the first place.

> For some reason I had it in my head that this.nuxt.options was the normalised config.

Doesn't really change my points but this statement is confusing. `this.nuxt.options` **is normalized**. Normalized built-in Nuxt options at least.
@rchl I think the point is that *both* are normalised, rather than just `this.nuxt.options`, which was my mistake.

from module perspective, this.nuxt.options.i18n is directly user input without applied defaults or normalization. We should only extend configuration (nuxtConfig) interface. I think confusion part is module type we exposed.

(note that I prefer that we talk about `this.options` rather than `this.nuxt.options` since `this.options` has well-defined type while `this.nuxt` is currently `any`)

> from module perspective, this.nuxt.options.i18n is directly user input without applied defaults or normalization.

Exactly. So `this.options.i18n` and `i18n` in `nuxt.config.js` should both have the same type. I can only achieve that currently if I extend `NuxtOptions` rather than `NuxtConfig`.

> We should only extend configuration (nuxtConfig) interface. I think confusion part is module type we exposed.

I don't think there is any confusion here. Rather either a bug in types or somehow conflicting recommendation that says that we should extend `NuxtConfig` always.

> I can only achieve that currently if I extend `NuxtOptions` rather than `NuxtConfig`.

Or extend both `NuxtOptions` and `NuxtConfig`, of course. But what would be the point of that if extending `NuxtOptions` alone have the same effect?
@rchl Because the `NuxtConfig` interface extends `NuxtOptions`, if you have augmented `NuxtOptions` you shouldn't need to augment `NuxtConfig` as well.

I know. At this point I'm only arguing with "We should only extend configuration (nuxtConfig) interface".

If we all agree that extending `NuxtOptions` is the way to go for modules so that the same types are applied to (for example) `this.options.i18n` in modules and `i18n` in `nuxt.config.js` then I have no more questions.

@rchl You are right. This is an issue with module typing. Extending nuxtConfig interface for i18n is correct. BTW this.options and this.nuxt.options are same references (if they don't have same type thats also an issue in typings)
